Who is credited with discovering Trisomy 18?
Trisomy 18: John H. Edwards. Trisomy 18, also known as Edwards syndrome, is a genetic disorder.
Who is credited with discovering Strontium?
Strontium: William Cruickshank. Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.

While working at a Soviet computing centre in 1985, this engineer created one of history's most popular video games — yet earned no royalties from it until founding a company with Henk Rogers in 1996. Who is he?
Alexey Pajitnov (born April 16, 1955) is a Russian and American computer engineer and video game designer.
This joint region where the foot meets the leg comprises three joints built from the talus, tibia, and fibula, enabling the foot's up-and-down flexing motions — what body part is it?
Ankle is the area where the foot and the leg meet.

Explicitly describing the relativity of motion and, by his own account, 23 years old in 499 CE, this figure is considered the first of the great mathematician-astronomers of classical Indian science — who is he?
Aryabhata (476-550 CE) was the first of the major mathematician-astronomers and early physicist from the classical age of Indian mathematics and Indian astronomy.
Causing frequent urination and a weak stream, this noncancerous enlargement of a male gland isn't caused by poor hygiene and has no known cure, only symptom management. What condition is it?
Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), also called prostate enlargement, is a noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland.
What hydrated mineral salt of sodium, mined economically in only a few places worldwide, forms a white crystalline solid that can be dehydrated by heating?
Borax (also referred to as sodium borate, tincal and tincar) is a salt (ionic compound) normally encountered as a hydrated borate of sodium, with the chemical formula Na2H20B4O17.
Atomic number 20 and chemically akin to strontium and barium, this metal is the most common ingredient in limestone — found there as its carbonate. What element?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
This set of metabolic reactions oxidizes biological fuels using an electron acceptor like oxygen to produce ATP, the molecule that stores usable chemical energy in cells — what is it?

Cellular respiration is the process of oxidizing biological fuels using an inorganic electron acceptor, such as oxygen, to drive production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which stores chemical energy in a biologically accessible form.

This genus of flowering trees and shrubs, native to South and East Asia, Melanesia, and Australia, gave rise through extensive hybridization to oranges, lemons, grapefruits, and limes — what's the genus called?
Citrus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the family Rutaceae.
A genus of over 260 fungi, most of them parasites that bore into insects and other arthropods, this 'club-headed' organism has 1,500 years of use in Chinese medicine — what is it?
Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.

Known by names ranging from the clinical to the crude to the childish — 'number two', 'dropping a deuce', 'doo-doo' — this basic biological process expels solid waste from the digestive tract. Name the process?

Defecation (or defaecation) follows digestion and is the necessary biological process by which organisms eliminate a solid, semisolid, or liquid waste material known as feces (or faeces) from the digestive tract via the anus or cloaca.

Massive enough to be rounded by its own gravity but too small to clear its orbital neighborhood like the solar system's eight major planets, Pluto became the prototype of this category after a 2006 reclassification. Name the category?

Dwarf planet is a small planetary-mass object that is in direct orbit around the Sun, massive enough to be gravitationally rounded, but insufficient to achieve orbital dominance like the eight classical planets of the Solar System.
This tightly coiled duct sits behind each testicle, serving as the crucial link to the vas deferens where sperm mature before their onward journey — what is it?
Epididymis (pl.: epididymides or) is an elongated tubular genital organ attached to the posterior side of each one of the two male reproductive glands, the testicles.
Which group of vascular plants, which reproduce via spores rather than seeds or flowers, are known for their large megaphyll leaves and the coiled 'fiddleheads' many species unfurl as new growth?
Fern (Polypodiopsida or Polypodiophyta) are a group of vascular plants (land plants with vascular tissues such as xylem and phloem) that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.
Reclassified twice before settling into its own genus, this Gram-variable, non-spore-forming coccobacillus is barely one to 1.5 micrometers across — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.
A friar, mathematician, and meteorologist who quietly worked out the laws of heredity with garden peas — and only got credit long after his death — who was this founder of genetics?
Gregor Mendel (20 July 1822 - 6 January 1884) was an Austrian biologist, meteorologist, mathematician, Augustinian friar and abbot of St.
This discipline governs the design and formal description ('blazon') of coats of arms, crests, and other armorial bearings — what is it called?
Heraldry (also known as armoury) is a discipline relating to the design, display, study and transmission of armorial bearings.
A person with this condition is excessively and unduly worried about having a serious illness, alarmed by even the most minor symptom — what is it?

Hypochondriasis is a condition in which a person is excessively and unduly worried about having a serious illness. International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10) classifies hypochondriasis as a mental and behavioral disorder.
Widely planted outside its native South America for its striking purple flowers, this tree is considered Vulnerable in the wild according to the IUCN — which species?
Jacaranda mimosifolia is a sub-tropical tree native to south-central South America that has been widely planted elsewhere because of its attractive and long-lasting violet-colored flowers.

This 20th-century Peruvian writer of mestizo descent composed novels, poems, and stories in both Spanish and Quechua, and even coined a new literary idiom to render Indigenous perspective more authentically — who is he?
José María Arguedas (Spanish) was a Peruvian novelist, poet, and anthropologist.
Which aromatic Mediterranean evergreen tree, prominent in classical Greco-Roman culture and used to season food, can grow up to 20 meters tall with smooth, glossy leaves?
Laurus nobilis is an aromatic evergreen tree or large shrub with green, glabrous (smooth) leaves.

This American four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft is a comprehensive update of an older Cold War-era design, and remains the only version of its lineage still in production, with 500 delivered to 26 operators. What aircraft is this?
Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules is a medium-size American four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
Often found combined with iron in minerals, this hard, brittle, silvery transition metal is added to stainless steel to improve strength and wear resistance. What element is it (symbol Mn)?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
This field of study examines and evaluates the procedures researchers use to gather and interpret data, rather than the findings those procedures produce — what is it called?
Methodology is the study of research methods.
First documented with ice cream and water by a Tanzanian student and his professor in the 1960s, this contested observation says warmer liquids can outrace colder ones to freezing — what's it called?
Mpemba effect is the observation that very hot liquids or colloids (such as ice cream) can freeze more quickly than colder ones, for similar volumes and surrounding conditions.

Discovered in a fossil-rich West African formation and first described in 1976 but not formally named until 1999, this rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur lived roughly 115 to 105 million years ago — which genus?
Nigersaurus is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived during the middle Cretaceous period, about 115 to 105 million years ago.
Chemists still debate the exact definition, but generally, any large molecule containing a carbon-hydrogen or carbon-carbon bond falls into this broad class of compounds. What is it?
Organic compound are a subclass of chemical compounds of carbon.
Made by grinding dry-roasted legumes and often tweaked with salt or emulsifiers, this protein-rich spread is the most popular of all the nut butters — what is it?
Peanut butter is a food paste or spread made from ground, dry-roasted peanuts.
Someone who specializes in matter, motion, and force through space and time earns the title 'physicist' — so what is the field they devote themselves to?
Physics is the scientific study of matter, its fundamental constituents, its motion and behavior through space and time, and the related entities of energy and force.
Which compound pulls double duty as a dietary iodine supplement and as the pill that protects the thyroid gland during radiation emergencies?
Potassium iodide (KI) is a chemical compound, medication, and dietary supplement.
A polyphenol from the flavonoid family with a naturally bitter taste, this compound turns up in capers and red onions and gets added to supplements — what is it?
Quercetin is a plant flavonol from the flavonoid group of polyphenols.
Holding a professorship in biology, neurology, and neurosurgery at Stanford, this primatologist is also a research associate with Kenya's National Museums — who is he?
Robert Sapolsky (born April 6, 1957) is an American academic, neuroscientist, and primatologist.
Which genus of large, tropical, many-legged predators takes its name from ancient Greek words meaning roughly 'thorn' and 'earthworm'?
Scolopendra (from Ancient Greek (sklops), meaning "thorn", and (nteron), meaning "earthworm") is a species-rich genus of large tropical centipedes of the family Scolopendridae.
Typically a bony enclosure around a vertebrate's brain, though cartilage in some fish and amphibians, this head structure combines a neurocranium with a facial skeleton — name it?

Skull is typically a bony enclosure around the brain of a vertebrate. In a human, the skull comprises two prominent parts: the neurocranium and the facial skeleton, which evolved from the first pharyngeal arch.
Often caused by a lesion narrowing an artery, as in atherosclerosis, this condition is sometimes also called a stricture or coarctation — what is it?
Stenosis (from Ancient Greek (stens) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.

A carnivorous marsupial formerly found across mainland Australia but now confined to Tasmania, this animal became the world's largest carnivorous marsupial after the thylacine's extinction in 1936. What is this fierce creature?
Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii; palawa kani: purinina) is a carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.
Tetrapods have these digits at the end of each limb; horses walk on their very tips in what's called an unguligrade stance — what are they?
Toe are the digits of the foot of a tetrapod.

This membrane-bound organelle, found in plant and fungal cells and some others, is essentially a water-filled storage compartment with no fixed shape, formed when smaller membrane vesicles fuse together. What is it called?
Vacuole is a membrane-bound organelle which is present in plant and fungal cells and some protist, animal, and bacterial cells.

Dubbed the "father of English geology," this man created the first detailed geological map of an entire country — yet his humble background got him snubbed by scientists and even landed him in debtors' prison. Who was he?
William Smith (geologist) (23 March 1769 - 28 August 1839) was an English geologist, credited with creating the first detailed, nationwide geological map of any country.
This painful collection of pus built up within body tissue often causes redness, warmth, and swelling, and includes boils and carbuncles as common types — what is it called?
Abscess: Localized collection of pus in body tissue. An abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
This wide-body twinjet shares its wing and much of its structure with the four-engined A340, and it first carried passengers for Air Inter in January 1994 — which aircraft is it?
About one-third the density of steel, this soft, nonmagnetic, silver-looking metal grows a protective oxide skin the instant it meets air — which element, symbol Al?
Aluminium: Chemical element with atomic number 13 (Al)
Triggered by either histamine or bradykinin, this rapid swelling of the deep skin layers can affect the face, tongue, or airway within minutes — what is it?
Angioedema: Disease characterized by rapid swelling.

Studying humanity's past through the recovery of artifacts and sites — including stone tools dating back 3.3 million years — this discipline sits at the crossroads of the social sciences and humanities — which field?
Archaeology: Study of human activity based on materials left behind.
Sold as Lipitor, this first-line statin lowers cholesterol to fend off cardiovascular disease, with mild muscle aches among its better-known side effects — what's the drug?
Named for the physicist who shared a 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie, this SI unit measures one radioactive decay event per second — which unit?
Becquerel: SI derived unit of radioactivity.
Despite its name, only the soles of this tawny, spotted feline's paws are actually dark — and at just 35 to 52 centimetres long, it ranks as Africa's smallest wild feline species — what animal is it?
Black-footed cat: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa.
Rooted in prehistoric herbalism for identifying edible and medicinal species, this branch of biology studies roughly 410,000 species of land plants — what field of study?
Named from the Greek word for butter, this oily, foul-smelling compound with the formula CH3CH2CH2COOH is a key component of the mammalian gut. What is it?
Butyric acid: Chemical compound (CH3CH2CH2COOH). It is an oily, colorless liquid with an unpleasant odor.
Also known as meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the Apiaceae family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — what is it?
Caraway: Species of plant in the carrot family.

Also known as gotu kola or Indian pennywort, this herbaceous perennial from the Apiaceae family is eaten as a vegetable and used in traditional medicine across Africa, Asia, and the Pacific — what is it?
Centella asiatica: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.

Nicknamed for its spider-like look and also called airplane plant or hen and chicks, this houseplant is native to tropical Africa but can suffer 'burnt tips' from fluoride in tap water — which species?
Chlorophytum comosum: Species of flowering plant. It is native to tropical and Southern Africa but has become naturalized in other parts of the world, including Western Australia and Bangladesh.
A shrub-like bush of western South America with oval leaves and small red berries, its leaves are chewed or brewed as a mild stimulant and famously contain a notorious alkaloid — which plant is it?
Coca: Plant in the Erythroxylaceae family.
This common bowel condition produces hard, infrequent stools and can lead to hemorrhoids or fecal impaction, with hypothyroidism and diabetes among its underlying causes. What is it?
Constipation: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements.

First described by Linnaeus in 1767, this citrus-family plant native to the Indian subcontinent has aromatic leaves essential to South Asian cooking, especially in India and Sri Lanka — which species?

Curry tree: Species of flowering plant. It is native to the Indian subcontinent, southern China and mainland Southeast Asia, and it has been introduced to other parts of southeast Asia and to Australia.
Nicknamed the 'gympie-gympie' by Queensland's Gubbi Gubbi people, this Australian and Malaysian rainforest plant delivers an infamously painful, long-lasting sting. What species is it?
Dendrocnide moroides: Species of plant in the nettle family.
Descended from the African wild ass and domesticated some 5,000 to 7,000 years ago, which working equine still numbers over 40 million worldwide?
Donkey: Domesticated animal primarily used for transportation.
Belonging to the order Anguilliformes and comprising roughly 1,000 species, these ray-finned predators transform dramatically from larva to adult and mostly live in salt water — what are they?
This fungal genus growing on rye and other cereals produces alkaloids that cause a poisoning condition in humans and livestock who eat contaminated grain — which group of fungi?
Ergot: Fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).

Its mating has never once been observed in the wild, and its five life stages were once mistaken for five separate species — this critically endangered fish is threatened by dams and overfishing. What is it?
European eel: Species of fish. The five stages of their development were originally thought to be different species.
Once tapped as a source of natural rubber, though no longer used commercially for that purpose, this houseplant native to South and Southeast Asia is nicknamed the 'rubber tree.' Which species?
Ficus elastica: Species of banyan tree.

One of the first management consultants, this American mechanical engineer wrote a 1909 book — later voted the most influential management book of the 20th century — and helped found industrial engineering. Who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor: American mechanical engineer (1856–1915)
This mathematician founded set theory and proved that there are more real numbers than natural numbers, revealing an infinity of infinities — who is he?
With DNA up to 99% identical to ours, this troop-dwelling great ape — led by a dominant 'silverback' — is the largest living primate on Earth — what is it?
Gorilla: Genus of large African apes.
This inherited disorder leaves blood unable to clot properly, causing prolonged bleeding after injury and, in its two main forms, low levels of clotting factor VIII or IX — which condition?
Haemophilia: Genetic disease involving blood clotting.

Governed by rules laid out in a document called a blazon, this medieval discipline of coats of arms, crests, and mottoes may have arisen so knights could recognize commanders behind their helmets — what is it?
Heraldry: Discipline of the design and study of coats of arms.
Running from your shoulder to your elbow, this long arm bone has a constriction nicknamed the 'surgical neck' due to its tendency to fracture — which bone?
Humerus: Long bone of the upper arm. It connects the scapula and the two bones of the lower arm, the radius and ulna, and consists of three sections.
This Russian-American engineer built the first successful four-engine aircraft in 1913 and went on to pioneer the modern helicopter — who was he?
Native to South America but planted worldwide for its long-lasting violet blooms, this tree — also called the black poui — is listed as Vulnerable in its wild range by the IUCN. What is it?
Jacaranda mimosifolia: Species of sub-tropical tree.
Court astronomer and advisor to Elizabeth I, this mathematician-occultist kept one of England's largest libraries and is credited with coining the term "British Empire" — who was he?
John Dee: English scientist and occultist (1527–1608/09)
Smaller, seedier, and more aromatic than its Persian cousin, this citrus hybrid lends its tart flavor to a beloved Florida pie named after the island chain it's associated with — what is it?
Key lime: Citrus fruit and plant.
Weighing up to 1,100 pounds, this heaviest of all non-crocodilian reptiles lacks a bony shell, its carapace covered instead in oily, leather-like flesh — what animal is it?
Leatherback sea turtle: Species of marine reptile.
Defined as exactly one cubic decimetre and rooted in an old French unit called the litron, what metric measure of volume is this?
Litre: Unit of volume. The litre (Commonwealth spelling) or liter (American spelling) (SI symbols L and l, other symbol used: ℓ) is a metric unit of volume.
Nicknamed the 'maker of modern Mysore,' this Indian civil engineer and statesman's birthday is now celebrated as Engineer's Day across India, Sri Lanka, and Tanzania — who is he?
M. Visvesvaraya: Indian civil engineer, administrator, and former prime minister of Mysore Kingdom.
Prized for its sweet, pine-and-citrus flavor, this perennial herb is often considered synonymous with oregano in parts of the Middle East — what is it?
Marjoram: Perennial herb. It is also called pot marjoram, although this name is also used for other cultivated species of Origanum.
The smallest planet in the Solar System is rocky with only a trace atmosphere, and its surface gravity is slightly higher than which other planet's?
Mercury is the first planet from the Sun and the smallest in the Solar System. It is a rocky planet with a trace atmosphere and a surface gravity slightly higher than that of Mars.
With over 17,000 built and flown by more than 50 countries, this Soviet-designed twin-turbine machine is the most-produced helicopter in the world — what is it?
Mil Mi-8: Family of transport helicopters.
Numbering roughly 160,000 species and mostly active at night, these insects share an order with butterflies but are known for their duller, darker wings — what are they?
Moth: Group of mostly-nocturnal insects in the order Lepidoptera.
The sole surviving family of an ancient cephalopod lineage, these nine living species carry coiled chambered shells 10 to 25 cm across and are all protected under CITES — what creatures are they?
Nautilus: Family of molluscs. It comprises nine living species in two genera, the type of which is the genus Nautilus.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and spread by the fecal-oral route, this is the most common cause of gastroenteritis — what is it?
Norovirus: Type of viruses that cause gastroenteritis.
Named after an ancient Greek city, this cactus genus is better known by its fruit's common name, the prickly pear, and goes by nopal or sabra in other cultures — what genus is it?
Opuntia: Genus of cactus. The plant has been introduced to Australia, southern Europe, the Middle East, and parts of Africa.
One researcher catalogued as many as 549 varieties of this psychological category, defined by intense arousal toward things that aren't sexual by nature — what is the term?
This order of hoofed mammals — horses, rhinos, and tapirs — bears its weight on an odd number of toes and digests plant fiber in its intestines rather than a multi-chambered stomach. Which order?
Perissodactyla: Order of hoofed mammals. Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek περισσός, perissós 'odd' and δάκτυλος, dáktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.
Domesticated twice in the Neolithic — once near the Tigris Basin and once in China — this even-toed, hoofed omnivore is farmed mainly for pork; what is it?

In this group of disorders, pigment-like substances called porphyrins accumulate in the body, triggering attacks of abdominal pain, confusion, and even seizures that can be set off by alcohol or fasting. What is it?
Porphyria: Metabolic disorders in which porphyrins build up in the body.
Nicknamed the 'liberty cap' for its distinctive conical shape, this psychoactive mushroom grows in grassland and produces psilocybin — what is it?
Psilocybe semilanceata: Species of fungus in the family Hymenogastraceae, native to Europe.
This Indian social activist founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan and later teamed with yoga guru Ramdev to promote swadeshi economics — who was he?
Rajiv Dixit: Indian activist. Rajiv Dixit (30 November 1967 – 30 November 2010) was an Indian social activist who founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan.
Holding Oxford's inaugural chair for the Public Understanding of Science, which outspoken atheist and evolutionary biologist wrote 'The Selfish Gene'?
Richard Dawkins: British evolutionary biologist and author (born 1941)
This extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period had closely-spaced eyes at the front of its head, 'like car headlamps,' and is best known from fossils found in Bolivia — what is it?
Sacabambaspis: Extinct genus of jawless fishes.
Distinguished from true seals by external ear flaps and the ability to walk on all fours, these marine mammals include a giant subspecies that can weigh up to 1,000 kilograms. What are they?
Sea lion: Subfamily of aquatic mammals.

No metal beats this one for electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, or reflectivity, and it's mostly mined as a byproduct of refining copper, gold, lead, and zinc — which element, symbol Ag, is it?
Silver: Chemical element with atomic number 47 (Ag)
Native to the Andes, this is the only living species in South America from the short-faced lineage, and unlike most of its relatives, eats mostly plants — which animal?
Spectacled bear: Species of mammal. The spectacled bear (Tremarctos ornatus), also known as the Andean bear, is a species of bear native to the Andes Mountains in northern and western South America.

Named from Greek words meaning 'a chain of berries' and 'pus-forming,' this Gram-positive bacterial species is the predominant carrier of the Lancefield group A antigen, often abbreviated GAS — what is this bacterium's full scientific name?
Streptococcus pyogenes: Species of bacterium. The name group A (beta-hemolytic) Streptococcus is thus also used.
This orange citrus fruit is usually considered a mandarin variety, though it's also thought to carry some pomelo ancestry — which fruit?

Born from 19th-century efforts to make steam engines more efficient — thanks largely to French physicist Sadi Carnot — this branch of physics is governed by four fundamental laws relating heat, work, and energy. What is it?

Thermodynamics: Physics of heat, work, and temperature. The initial application of thermodynamics to mechanical heat engines was quickly extended to the study of chemical compounds and chemical reactions.

Once dismissed as rare and bizarre, this childhood-onset disorder pairs multiple motor tics with at least one vocal tic, often heralded by a premonitory urge the person can briefly suppress — what's it called?
Tourette syndrome: Neurodevelopmental disorder involving motor and vocal tics.
Often caused by poor circulation or prolonged pressure on the skin, this open sore — also known as a bedsore when linked to immobility — can destroy tissue down to the fat layer. What is it called?

First glimpsed through Dmitri Ivanovsky's 1892 study of an ailing tobacco plant, this is the most numerous biological entity on Earth — yet it can only replicate inside another organism's living cells. What is it?
Virus: Infectious agent that replicates in cells.
This American child prodigy entered Harvard at 11 and lectured on four-dimensional geometry at 12 before deliberately retreating from public life — who was he?
William James Sidis: American mathematician, polyglot, and child prodigy (1898–1944)
Iron is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for iron is Fe. Iron is a chemical element; it has symbol Fe and atomic number 26.
Plutonium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for plutonium is Pu. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.

Ray Liotta: Raymond Allen Liotta ( lee-OH-tə, Italian: [liˈɔtta]; December 18, 1954 – May 26, 2022) was an American actor.
In what year was Julia Louis-Dreyfus born?
Julia Louis-Dreyfus: Julia Scarlett Elizabeth Louis-Dreyfus ( LOO-ee DRY-fəss; born January 13, 1961) is an American actress, comedian, and producer.

Joe Alwyn: Joseph Matthew Alwyn (born 21 February 1991) is an English actor.

Michael B. Jordan: Michael Bakari Jordan ( bah-KAR-ee; born February 9, 1987) is an American actor, producer, and director.

Sandra Bullock: Sandra Annette Bullock (born July 26, 1964) is an American actress and film producer.

Sting (musician): Gordon Matthew Thomas Sumner (born 2 October 1951), known as Sting, is an English musician, songwriter and actor.

Angus Cloud: Conor Angus Cloud Hickey (July 10, 1998 – July 31, 2023) was an American actor.

Alan Rickman: Alan Sidney Patrick Rickman (21 February 1946 – 14 January 2016) was an English actor.
In what year did Charles Bronson die?
Charles Bronson (born Charles Dennis Buchinsky; November 3, 1921 – August 30, 2003) was an American actor.
In what year was Aliens first released?
Aliens is a 1986 science fiction-action film written and directed by James Cameron.
In what year was Ghostbusters first released?
Ghostbusters is a 1984 American supernatural comedy film directed by Ivan Reitman and written by Dan Aykroyd and Harold Ramis.
In what year was The Out-Laws first released?
The Out-Laws was released by Netflix on July 7, 2023.
In what year was Avatar: The Last Airbender first released?
Avatar: The Last Airbender: 2005. It won five Annie Awards, a Genesis Award, a Primetime Emmy Award, a Kids' Choice Award, and a Peabody Award.
In what year was Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour first released?
Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour: 2023. Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour is a 2023 American concert film produced by the singer-songwriter Taylor Swift and directed by Sam Wrench.
In what year was Zero Dark Thirty first released?
Zero Dark Thirty is a 2012 American political action thriller film directed by Kathryn Bigelow and written by Mark Boal.
In what year was The Departed first released?
The Departed is a 2006 crime thriller film, directed by Martin Scorsese and written by William Monahan.
In what year was Apocalypto first released?
